about: Read-only survey of every unread outcome-web link on main, Oct 29 (laws lead, effects-web-survey workflow): one row per link with status, owning engine, read point, cause, size, smallest build, effort, risks and the evidence read. The plan is effects-web-plan-2026-10-29.md; the critic corrections are applied there, not here.

surveys.group: schools: the 11 links in src/core2/data/outcome-web/unwired.json under SG-SCHOOL-links-not-running (7), SG-SCHOOL-hispanic-enrollment (1), SG-WEB-unread-school-graduation-pct (1), SG-WEB-unread-school-reading-proficient-pct (1) and SG-SCHOOL-college-completion (1). Read on main at 01b2ca6c55. Cross-cutting findings: (a) the school engine already multiplies by the web's factor for graduation and reading (src/core2/school-outcomes.ts:317-323, decideSchoolOutcome calls webReach for every income fifth). So for housing-vouchers-to-graduation and library-materials-to-reading the only blocker is a size, and the replacement text in their SG-WEB-unread stopgaps (stopgaps.json:7019, :7031), which asks for that read, is stale. (b) A student's immigration status is now partly on the record: citizenship.ts:32 isUnauthorized, seeded per person at both tiers, already read for the 287(g) law at jobs-web.ts:228-246. So "no student immigration status" in SG-SCHOOL-links-not-running and in the daca row's notes is stale. One caveat: children get the adult citizen share. (c) lead-to-reading's size 0.26 comes from the 2016 NBER working paper's 3.1 points. The published AEJ: Applied abstract gives 0.96 points on a 12% base, about +8%. (d) PR #6808 (claude/laws-college-step) edits school-outcomes.ts (+304 lines), law-wiring-schools-web.test.ts, stopgaps.json and unwired.json, so every other schools PR lands after it.

surveys.familyProposal:
Order: PR #6808 (college step) merges first, because it rewrites school-outcomes.ts, law-wiring-schools-web.test.ts, stopgaps.json and unwired.json. Every other schools PR merges main after it.

Family 1, school grades. Data only; the reader is decideSchoolOutcome at school-outcomes.ts:317, which already reads the web. Two PRs while the owner is awake (owner, Oct 27), one link each:
(1a) housing-vouchers-to-graduation graded about-zero (Jacob/Kapustin/Ludwig 2015; Schwartz et al. 2020 is test scores only).
(1b) library-materials-to-reading graded about-zero, estimated from Gilpin/Karger/Nencka 2024 and the ALA 2023 share.
Each PR regenerates the effect matrix and runs write-unwired.ts; its ABOUT_ZERO path resolves SG-WEB-unread-school-graduation-pct and SG-WEB-unread-school-reading-proficient-pct. Each also updates the pin at law-wiring-schools-web.test.ts:362-372. Effort S each.
The same family can carry two data corrections with no wiring: lead-to-reading's size moves to the published AEJ figure (0.96 points on a 12% base, about 0.08), and the stale 'no student immigration status' text in SG-SCHOOL-links-not-running and the daca row is fixed, since citizenship.ts now records status.

Family 2, the moves engine (counted-moves.ts leavingOf and arrivals; moves.ts webLeavingFor): enforcement-to-hispanic-enrollment, carried as a person-level twin for mixed-status households. Its status comes from citizenship.ts isUnauthorized, as jobs-web.ts already reads it for the same law. Start it only after people-protected-traits-on-record adds Hispanic origin (owner ruling Oct 24). Effort L.

Family 3, per-student exposure reads in decideSchoolOutcome. Each link waits on another engine's record, so each lands as one PR when its record exists, never as a school-side stand-in:
- class-size-to-scores: the district pupil-teacher ratio from teacher jobs, plus a staffing decision. Guard against double counting school-spending-to-attainment.
- lead-to-reading: blood lead in the health engine. Redirect pool item outcome-causes-health-programs away from a web-ledger outcome.
- heat-to-learning: a weather record in the disasters engine under the Oct 16 ruling, shared with heat-to-deaths. Redirect outcome-causes-housing-disaster-justice the same way.
- daca-to-graduation: a federal executive deferred-action row.

Park with stopgaps kept: homicide-nearby-to-scores and police-killing-to-graduation. Both need a home location below the place, and their place-level effect is about zero.

Family 4, schoolDay (src/core2/modules/school.ts): carbon-monoxide-to-absence. Read the Currie et al. 2009 table first. At 2026 CO levels it most likely grades about-zero as a data-only PR; only if it does not, record county CO from EPA AirData and add a stay-home term in schoolDay.

critique:
**Coverage:** all 59 links in `unwired.json` on origin/main (55e28f6688) are in the plan's table, with no duplicates and no extras. The matrix summary on main matches the plan's starting point (169 reach, 18 about zero, 59 fail). Corrections:

1. **One unread link is hidden from `unwired.json`.** licensing-reform-to-poverty counts as reaching only because its `carriedBy` text is not empty. That text reads "none yet: no engine path (stopgap SG-WEB-poverty-licensing-no-engine)".
   - Evidence: `coverage.json:464-466`. `effect-matrix.ts:287-291` (reachPoint) passes any `carriedBy` that is not empty. Nothing in `src/core2` reads occupational licensing; the only hit is the `api.stopgap` call at `outcome-web.ts:643`. Pool item world-licensing-reform-jobs is open.
   - Family 1 already fixes the same stale text on graduation-to-poverty. It should also clear licensing's `carriedBy` and close SG-WEB-poverty-graduation-no-engine, which is still open and stale. The plan leaves that stopgap out.
   - The honest starting point is 168 reaching, 18 about zero, 60 unread.

2. **"wire" is wrong for drug-negotiation-to-out-of-pocket.**
   - The read point (`billMembers` in `medical-bills.ts`) exists only on `claude/laws-medical-debt`.
   - Drugs are part of the one everyday-living amount: `LivingPlan` in `cost-of-living.ts` has only a sellers map and `monthlyMinor`, no categories (`living-costs-data.ts` drugs $658). So taking drugs out of everyday living is a new split.
   - The cause can never change in play. `federal-answers.json` lists only two questions and has no law row for this one, so `lawValue` (`outcome-web.ts:200`) reads 0. The survey's "in force everywhere at the opening" is wrong.
   - Background Congress cannot propose federal-only questions (SG-GOV-federal-proposal-coverage, `world-legislating.ts:945-946`).
   - Correct status: needs a record, and blocked on gov-federal-questions-answers-stances.

3. **"wire" is wrong for container-deposit-to-litter.**
   - No engine records litter (`outcome-web-environment-carried.test.ts:91-102`).
   - The business loop in place-prices that it would join runs only inside the energy price rule (`place-prices.ts:1393`, `if (rule.kind === "share")`). It needs a new loop and a new ESTIMATED parameter from an industry-funded study.
   - Its lag is 12 months. A law enacted on day 2 of a one-year run reads nothing before the run ends (`causeAt`, #6006).
   - Correct status: needs a record, effort M, and its proof needs a run of at least 13 months.

4. **The other wire and carried claims hold, with caveats.**
   - **federal-deficit:** holds (`interestFactor` at `budgets-treasury.ts:234/1122`; the `defenseBoostPct` pattern at `gov-measures.ts:371`).
     - `legislatedBudget` in `budgets.ts` changes `spendingMinor` only, so the reader sees spending bills, never tax changes. Register that as a stopgap.
     - Its files are `gov-measures.ts`, `outcome-web.ts` ENGINE_READERS, `outcome-web.json` and `links.json`, not `budgets-treasury.ts`.
   - **relief-to-votes:** holds (`candidateReasons` at `electorate-inputs.ts:126`; `rt.paid` at `disasters.ts:66` has no date).
     - With the down-ballot share at 0, the first race that reads it is November 2028, so its proof is a run of about four years, not one.
     - `electorate-inputs.ts` is a "knowing" reader in the matrix (`effect-matrix.ts:55`), so it counts only through `carriedBy`.
   - **graduation-to-earnings and rent-burden-to-homelessness (carried):** hold (`jobs.ts:2595-2649` schoolingOn, graduationOf, collegeOf; `housing-homeless.ts:351-404`).
   - **eviction-to-hospital-visits and coverage-to-catastrophic-bills:** both leave out the counted tier. On the branch, counted care need is illness 1 or 0 (`medical-bills.ts:321`), and counted Medicaid adults are billed as uninsured. Each needs a registered stopgap or a build under "one model, two tiers".

5. **The "quiet causes" note is wrong for heat and water.** Hot days and water violations do not drift.
   - SG-WEB-outcome-drift holds every kept outcome at its base.
   - Nothing in `src/core2` records `env.hot-days` or `env.drinking-water-violations`, and no `links.json` row has either as its outcome.
   - Their factor is exactly 1 in every played world. Families 8 and 9 would build records (the born-small row, the heat cause row) that move nobody. The water-violations producer item is dropped.
   - Also missing from the quiet list:
     - rail: federal-only question, 30-month lag;
     - drug negotiation: never in force;
     - relief: first reading race is November 2028;
     - litter: 12-month lag;
     - federal-loan-cap (in flight): federal-only question.

6. **Family 9 gains +1, not "+1 or +2".**
   - The matrix follows chains only through `from` (`FROM` at `effect-matrix.ts:351-355`), never through moderators.
   - energy-price-to-ac-use has no size, so the web does not run it.
   - Section 8 doesn't add up: 194 + 23 + 28 = 245, not 246.

7. **Project rules: workflow step 2 breaks "builders build; checkers check".** AGENTS.md on origin/main (line 84, Oct 29 ruling) says builders and their helpers run only the test files they wrote or changed. Typecheck, the guards, the gate, zero-dice and speed:year belong to the checker. The rule also says to message the checker; a PR comment is only the backup. The capacity plan built around the builder running a full typecheck goes away with this.

8. **Capacity leaves out disk.**
   - `/` has 3.9 GB free (91% used).
   - `/home/user/h-lenders` is a full 3.3 GB copy. The Oct 29 rule says to narrow it at once (`helper-checkout.sh narrow`).
   - `/home/user/wf-crime` (1.1 GB) still serves #6792, which has merged.

   - Family 6 says to claim gov-justice-counted-dispositions first. That item comes `after: gov-justice-counted-incidents`, which is open and unclaimed, so coordinate in its Notes rather than claim it.
   - Family 6's new reclassification question is a player-facing bill that is not in `political-process-baseline.md` (it says only that courts come after early access). Add it to the CTO's scope list.
   - The 56 starting rows for larceny (Prop 47, SQ 780, NCSL) are research that section 5 leaves out.
   - Family 3's list of files leaves out `medical-bills.ts`.
   - Section 6 calls federal minimums "parked"; the table says "blocked".
   - library-materials-to-reading has no study at all, so grading it about zero is an estimate rounded to zero. That needs a different CTO ruling from "statistically insignificant means zero".
   - congress-stock-ban's anchor must name the contrary finding (Wei and Zhou 2025, leaders outperform).

10. **Time.** At the plan's own rates the families come to about 60 agent-hours (about 30 per lane). That is before waiting on #6763, the medical-debt branch, the births helper and the research PR. It also leaves out the multi-year proofs: about four years for relief, about 16 for birth-year air, 10 or more for gas hookups, 2.5 or more for rail. Each runs at about 2 minutes per game year, times a twin, times two draws, under one lock. Four to five working days is the realistic estimate.
